stagingDisclosure: Fictional editorial test story. Illustrated staging; not a real user submission.
title: THE SPARE KEY
hook: My sister has let herself in despite our agreement. She asks to stay on the night I promised my partner privacy.

evidenceFacts.claim: My adult sister had a spare key during my night work; we agreed she would ask before coming over.
Her coat and school bag were on the chair; she had used the key without asking and gone back to the hallway; she took evening classes.
I held my own phone; her message read “I’m in the hallway. Please don’t tell Mum I’m here.”
She had reported an argument with Mum earlier, without saying why.
In the building hallway my sister stood outside my door and asked, “Can I stay tonight?”
I promised my partner the flat to ourselves before an early medical appointment; my partner was not home yet.
I did not know if my sister had anywhere else safe to go.
My sister said she could wait while I thought inside; I could return; belongings stayed on the chair and I retained the phone.
I could invite her now, ask what happened before agreeing, or decline tonight and offer to help find somewhere.
Her answer and the availability of another place were unknown.
I wanted her safe and wanted to keep both promises; I had not agreed to a stay.

tension.protect: My sister’s safety, my partner’s promised privacy, and a boundary about access to our home.
tension.description: Belongings are already inside, but consent to staying has not happened. A request at the threshold does not cancel the promise inside.

poles.motive: Offer immediate shelter to someone close whose alternatives I do not know.
Honor a specific promise and avoid treating a key as unlimited permission.

tension.ethicalAsymmetry: Neither family loyalty nor the partner’s appointment licenses inventing danger or trivializing privacy. The key agreement was crossed; the source supports that problem, not a verdict about the sister’s character. Declining is attractive because of real promises, but offering help does not guarantee safety. Asking is a consequential conditional response, not a free optimization step.
tension.whyNow: It is my apartment access and my promise; my sister directly asks me before a stay is agreed. The absent partner also has a claim, but cannot be puppeted into endorsing my answer.
tension.power: I can consent to entry and offer help; I do not control available lodging. My sister holds physical access, not unlimited permission. The partner’s claim comes from the shared promise, not a depicted threat.
unknowns: Why the argument with Mum happened; no allegation of abuse is established.
Whether my sister had somewhere else safe.
Whether alternative accommodation would be possible.
Why she used the key without asking.
Whether asking would supply enough information to decide.
Why she needs to stay this night beyond the unexplained argument.

scenes.entryState: I know our key agreement and find belongings inside my home. My phone is in hand. I have not heard the stay request.

arc.change: The chair contains her things; my phone locates her outside and asks for secrecy from Mum.
arc.understanding: Presence inside the flat and consent to a stay are separate. An unexplained argument cannot supply a danger story.
arc.nextSceneReason: Go to the person in the hallway, where the request can be heard directly.
arc.removalLoss: Without this frame the key boundary disappears; the situation becomes a generic request for a bed.

scenes.exitState: Message delivered; objects stay on chair; phone remains held; hallway portal enabled.

scenes.entryState: I carry my phone to my sister; belongings remain inside. I know the argument is unexplained.

arc.change: She asks to stay. I remember my promise before an early appointment. She explicitly permits a thinking interval inside.
arc.understanding: The second claim on the flat is concrete; I cannot infer either a safe alternative or an emergency.
arc.nextSceneReason: A return inside lets me occupy the place I promised without inventing partner dialogue. It is a supported reflection interval.
arc.removalLoss: Without the direct request the primary act has no physical target; without permission, returning could imply abandonment.

scenes.exitState: Request delivered once; sister remains at waiting mark; reflection portal enabled.

scenes.entryState: I return inside to think with permission; sister remains outside; partner is absent; phone and chair objects retain ownership.

arc.change: Nothing new has happened while I think. The occupied chair now sits in the flat I promised to keep private.
arc.understanding: A pause cannot solve missing knowledge. Asking first, inviting now, and declining with an offer are three different initial acts.
arc.nextSceneReason: Select one act; approach the same hallway threshold reversibly; confirm there; author account follows.
arc.removalLoss: Without this return the two claims are explained but less materially co-present. Cut if the extra visit yields no understanding/care.

scenes.exitState: Exactly one act accepted at the threshold target, with sister unchanged; author encounter follows.

portals.phase: first request, then reversible thinking interval

observations.label: Notice the chair
observations.physicalNotice: Her coat and school bag sit on the chair. Author context confirms she came in with the key without asking, then went back to the hall; the objects alone do not prove how she entered. There is no readable label, contents or clue about the argument.
observations.spatialBenefit: Things inside establish access before permission to stay; the chair is occupied without the person.
observations.discoverability: The occupied chair is the first midground silhouette beside my entry path; an ordinary focus bracket names Notice the chair.
observations.accessibleEquivalent: Her coat and school bag sit on the chair. Author context confirms she came in with the key without asking, then went back to the hall; the objects alone do not prove how she entered. There is no readable label, contents or clue about the argument.

observations.label: Read her message
observations.physicalNotice: On my own phone: “I’m in the hallway. Please don’t tell Mum I’m here.” Only this message is shown.
observations.spatialBenefit: The screen points attention from absent belongings to the adjacent threshold, while I retain a private communication of my own.
observations.discoverability: The phone is already in my hand; readable actions include Read her message.
observations.accessibleEquivalent: On my own phone: “I’m in the hallway. Please don’t tell Mum I’m here.” Only this message is shown.

preparations.label: Go back to the threshold
preparations.effect: Move only the hero to the doorway and restore the held two-shot; request is not replayed.
preparations.undo: Step back into the flat before accepting an act.

opportunities.label: Invite her to stay tonight
opportunities.motive: Give immediate shelter rather than require an explanation first.
opportunities.physicalEnactment: Auto-approach the inside threshold before confirmation; on accept hero faces sister and begins the invitation gesture. The door does not move and she does not cross.
opportunities.confirmationCopy: Invite my sister to stay tonight now? This agrees to a stay; her response and entry are not simulated.
opportunities.finalPose: Hero facing sister at inside threshold, phone held, doorway unchanged.
opportunities.stopFrame: Invitation intention caption delivered, before sister movement or reply.

opportunities.label: Ask what happened before agreeing
opportunities.motive: Seek needed information while making no promise yet.
opportunities.physicalEnactment: Hero approaches then addresses sister, phone held. Caption: “You ask what happened before agreeing to a stay.” This ends the attempt; no answer unlock.
opportunities.confirmationCopy: Ask what happened before agreeing to a stay? Your version ends at the question. You will not receive a simulated answer or choose again.
opportunities.finalPose: Hero speaking toward sister, no beckoning or doorway closing.
opportunities.stopFrame: Question intention delivered before sister’s answer or a second decision.

opportunities.label: Say tonight cannot work; offer to help find somewhere
opportunities.motive: Protect the promise without simply abandoning the sister.
opportunities.physicalEnactment: Hero addresses sister at threshold with an open neutral hand. No phone search, booking or eviction animation.
opportunities.confirmationCopy: Say tonight cannot work and offer to help find somewhere? This is an offer, not a guarantee that another safe place exists.
opportunities.finalPose: Hero facing sister, phone retained; sister stays at original mark.
opportunities.stopFrame: Decline-and-help intention caption delivered, before acceptance, leaving, lodging search or door closure.

stopFrames.invite_now: Invitation intention caption delivered, before sister movement or reply.
stopFrames.ask_first: Question intention delivered before sister’s answer or a second decision.
stopFrames.decline_help: Decline-and-help intention caption delivered, before acceptance, leaving, lodging search or door closure.

worldPersistence.initial: Hero in living with owned phone; sister in threshold; coat and bag remain location-owned in living as placed belongings. Sister’s spare key is a fact only, not simulated inventory. Partner and Mum are offstage references in facts, never actors spawned nearby.
worldPersistence.transitions: Hero alone transfers to threshold for first request and returns to living to think. Phone follows hero by ownership; chair, coat and bag stay inside. Sister does not come inside, leave or handle belongings.
worldPersistence.returnInvariant: Revisiting living restores the occupied chair and phone message. Revisiting hall preserves sister’s waiting mark and consumed request; no repeat question, new message or Mum call. F08 permission persists. Final-phase actions remain available from inside-threshold mark or readable view.
worldPersistence.end: Choosing invite does not transfer sister; choosing decline does not evict her; choosing ask does not set an answer fact. Accepted act freezes the situation before these counterfactual changes.
worldPersistence.decisionReadyRule: Derive decisionPhase=ready only when the final decision phase is entered, all primaryDecision.minimumKnowledge facts have receipts, and no act is accepted. Cancel preserves readiness; acceptance closes all opportunities atomically. A final-phase location revisit does not rewind the arc.

presentation.compositionBrief: Living: chair silhouettes visibly occupy a place while its person is absent; phone insert reveals only own received message. Hall: sister on hall floor, hero on living-side edge, jamb between. Return: matching chair arrangement, phone retained, open sightline toward waiting sister. A threshold-facing crop can show the sister through the door without changing her registered location. On mobile preserve chair-to-door relation using two composed crops, not extra scenes.
presentation.specialProjectionRule: k_return remains the primary scene and living is the hero’s location. Auto-approach goes only to an inside_threshold mark in living; sister stays registered in threshold and is visible across the portal. This adjacent visible actor is a projection, never duplicate ownership. Revisiting threshold after F08 projects the same final decision phase; request is not replayed and all three acts stay reachable from the action list. No new scene, second request or offscreen dialogue is introduced.

controls.structure: One threshold tableau and two reader-paced frames. First: labeled earlier-inside recollection showing the chair and own-phone message. Second: direct stay request, promise, permission to think and all available options. Phone insert remains in the parent location; no third location.
controls.preserved: F01–F11, both initial observations, all three acts, identical uncertainty/confirmation/reveal. Earlier geography remains explicit in words and illustration.
controls.removed: Walking out and back; separate living-room decision view. Auto-approach is unnecessary because hero begins at threshold.
controls.hypothesis: The rich return may make the promise about the flat tangible and distinguish access from consent. If the threshold already communicates both, keep the short version.
